intro: One cedar, and a resemblance that made it famous. Seen from the field below, Kosugi no Osugi's two rounded crowns read as a pair of ears, and since about 2020 visitors have arrived with umbrellas to recreate a scene from an animated film. The village knew it first as Meoto-sugi, the married-couple cedar, its trunk split into two cores since a village monument listing in 1986. Somewhere between 700 and 1,000 years old, free, about half an hour by car from Shinjo Station.
meta_description: Kosugi no Osugi, the Totoro Tree of Sakegawa: two rounded crowns read as ears. 700 to 1,000 years old, a village monument since 1986. Free.
question_meta: Sakegawa's mapped tree is Kosugi no Osugi, known as the Totoro Tree, put at 700 to 1,000 years old.
question_answer: Sakegawa's mapped tree is Kosugi no Osugi, a Japanese cedar known internationally as the Totoro Tree because its two rounded crowns, seen from the field below, resemble the ears of the animated character. Its age is genuinely disputed: Japanese Wikipedia gives 700 to over 800 years, while Yamagata Prefecture's own landscape register heads its entry with an estimate of 1,000, and neither source states a method.
question_context: The trunk divides into two cores just above the base, which is why the village has long called it Meoto-sugi, the married-couple cedar, and Enmusubi no Sugi, the matchmaking cedar; a mountain deity is enshrined at its foot, and one local story has a lord of Shinjo sheltering under it from a blizzard while deer hunting. From around 2020 the tree's resemblance to a character from a well-known animated film turned it into an international destination, with visitors posing beneath it holding umbrellas. Its age is disputed: Japanese Wikipedia gives 700 to over 800 years, while Yamagata Prefecture's own landscape register heads the entry with an estimate of 1,000, and neither source states a method, so the honest range spans both. Its base measures 6.3 metres round, it stands about 20 metres tall, and its crown spans roughly 17 metres. Sakegawa Village listed it as a natural monument in November 1986. There is a public car park and a marked path from it, about half an hour by car from JR Shinjo Station; the path is not cleared in winter.

trees.name: Kosugi no Osugi (the Totoro Tree)

location.address: 108-5 Magarikawa, Sakegawa Village, Mogami District, Yamagata Prefecture

trees.story:
People arrive at this cedar carrying umbrellas, so they can stand underneath and recreate a scene from an animated film. From the field below, the tree's two rounded crowns read as a pair of ears, and from about 2020 that resemblance turned a cedar in a village of northern Yamagata into a destination people fly in for.

The village had always read the same shape differently. The trunk divides into two cores just above the base, so the tree has long been Meoto-sugi, the married-couple cedar, and Enmusubi no Sugi, the matchmaking cedar. A mountain deity is enshrined at its foot. One local story has a lord of Shinjo, out hunting deer, sheltering under it from a blizzard.

The age is genuinely disputed. Japanese Wikipedia gives 700 to over 800 years. Yamagata Prefecture's own landscape register heads the entry with an estimate of 1,000. Neither states a method, so the honest answer is somewhere between seven hundred and a thousand years and nobody has narrowed it. The dimensions are firmer: 6.3 metres around the base, about 20 metres tall, a crown roughly 17 metres across.

Sakegawa Village listed it as a natural monument in November 1986. It is free, with a car park and a marked path, about half an hour by car from Shinjo station and no closer by train. The path is not cleared in winter, and this part of Yamagata gets a great deal of snow.
trees.access: Free, a village-designated natural monument with a public car park and marked path; Japanese Wikipedia notes the path from the car park to the tree is not snow-cleared in winter, implying open, unstaffed access the rest of the year
trees.transport: No direct train or bus found; nearest station is JR Shinjo (Ou Main Line / Yamagata Shinkansen terminus), about 30 minutes by car or taxi from there
